Multisample GC/MS deconvolution, alignment and shared spectral recovery

Source: R/GCMS_batch.R
GCMSbatch.Rd

Supply a directory to gcmsDeco() to process an experiment. Sample group subdirectories are retained, and standards/ contains alkane calibrations. The closest standard in acquisition time calibrates each sample. Results share spectra through logconNMF::logconNMF() while keeping original scan grids.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
fitted(object, sample = 1L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
coef(object, sample = NULL, normalize = c("none", "l1"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
plot(x, sample = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
logLik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
GIC(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
AIC(object, ..., k = 2)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
BIC(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
EBIC(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
MBIC(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'GCMSbatch'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

sample

One sample index or identifier. NULL in coef() returns the common spectral library. NULL in plot() plots the coupled area table.

...

Arguments passed to the corresponding sample or coupled method.

normalize

Spectrum normalization: unnormalized or unit L1.

x, object

A multisample result returned by gcmsDeco().

k

Information-criterion multiplier.

Value

A GCMSbatch object with samples, optional coupled fit, sample RDS paths, consensus areas, reusable channel_groups, the parallel thread allocation, output files and stage timings. Use readRDS(x$paths[i]) for a full per-sample gcmsDeco() object.

Details

Directory layout can be experiment/standards/alkanes.cdf, experiment/beer1/sample001.cdf, and experiment/beer2/sample002.cdf. Analytical samples are sorted by acquisition timestamp, including its time zone. The exported CDF timestamp is never used as an acquisition date. If acquisition dates are absent, pass explicit relative sample paths in batch=list(sample_order=...).

batch supports method="cosine" or "hellinger", align=TRUE, coupling=list() for logconNMF::logconNMF() controls, sample_order=NULL, exposure=NULL, resume=FALSE, plots=FALSE, workers=NULL and cache=TRUE. workers limits concurrent samples within the total ncores budget. cache controls the aggregated-observation RAM cache during coupled fitting. exposure may be a positive scalar, a list with one scan-wise vector per acquisition-ordered sample, or a function of a sample's metadata and time vector. The default preserves vendor intensities. Known integration durations are appropriate when the data are integrated ion counts. Sequential full-scan mass spectrometers allocate acquisition time over m/z; exported peak counts and retained traces do not identify the per-mass dwell time. No automatic division by the number of exported channels is applied.

Samples run concurrently with their own sparse PSF and smooth background. A common channel map is learned from summed, time-binned chromatograms; pass a saved logconNMF::channelGroups() map as precluster to reuse reference groups. Matching uses the shared aggregate space. Original-channel means and the likelihood are used for coupled updates. Shared spectra are exported on the union of recorded mass ranges; unmeasured channels receive zero likelihood weight. Missing compounds retain NA areas. No gap filling is performed. coupled=FALSE keeps the independently fitted results.

The output directory contains per-sample MSP, Excel and fitted RDS files, an acquisition-ordered samples.csv, areas.csv, a consensus MSP library, and experiment.xlsx with samples, compounds, areas and packed spectra. batch=list(plots=TRUE) also writes each sample's trace and heatmap PDFs. Observations and factors are stored per sample, enabling streamed fitting; only aggregate observations are cached across samples in RAM, and the returned object contains paths, tables and compact common spectra. Original-channel spectral/background updates read blocks of at most 32 channels. Each active independent fit has its own temporary working buffers; these are released before the next assigned sample. A 10,000-by-32 cache needs 2.56 MB per sample, or 2.56 GB for 1,000 samples, in addition to worker and factor memory. Keep the output directory with the saved object. Explicit resume=TRUE reuses independent fits only when the file metadata and fitting arguments match; coupled refinement is recomputed.

See also

gcmsDeco(), logconNMF::logconNMF(), writeGCMSCDF()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
experiment <- gcmsDeco("chromatograms", output_dir="results",
  family=quasipoisson("identity"), precluster=32L,
  batch=list(method="hellinger",plots=TRUE))
experiment$areas
plot(experiment,sample=1,type="lines")
} # }
